reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from the toolkit rather than from the row. Psalm 22 is a title=MT-v1 psalm, so web:Ps.22.N = oshb:Ps.22.N+1; all three dual-cites carry correct arithmetic (0+1=1, 1+1=2, 3+1=4) and the web:Ps.22.0 = oshb:Ps.22.1 title pseudo-ref is the owner-ruled form. The one Hebrew quote collates at BYTE tier against the ref it cites (collate.py, tier "byte") and is verse-initial there: וְאַתָּ֥ה קָד֑וֹשׁ opens oshb:Ps.22.4 (= web:Ps.22.3). The span's cohesion claim holds in both witnesses: the WEB tokens you/your appear in 5 of 5 verses across web:Ps.22.1-Ps.22.5, and MT carries בְּ֭ךָ at oshb:Ps.22.5 and אֵלֶ֣יךָ at oshb:Ps.22.6. The 5|6 seam is a genuine addressee shift, not a taste call: MT opens oshb:Ps.22.7 with the contrastive וְאָנֹכִ֣י and WEB reads “But I am a worm, and no man” (web:Ps.22.6), with the you/your sweep returning 0 of 3 verses across web:Ps.22.6-Ps.22.8. The selah absence is inventory-true: pmarks_Ps.json records 71 selah verses book-wide and carries no Ps.22 key, and the claim is scoped to the row's own parent psalm. The poetry_lines figures are accurate as stated (3 at Ps.22.14; 1 at each of Ps.22.1-Ps.22.5), though that field is WEB layout and carries no boundary weight — the row offers it as observation and rests the boundary on addressee continuity, which is the right ordering. Confidence high is calibrated.

The span is right and I do not contest it: the you/your sweep returns 0 of 3 verses across web:Ps.22.6-Ps.22.8, so the description-mode unit really is bounded by the address units on either side, and both dual-cites are arithmetically correct (6+1=7, 8+1=9). What I contest is the warrant the row elects. It names WEB quotation punctuation as the tier-1 device, and that device is single-witness: the MT bytes at the seam carry no speech-introducing verb, and the staged source has no quotation layer at all. An OL-grade frame was available one clause away in the jussive chain, which is what the row should have cited. The seam survives the defect, so the severity is low and the repair is a warrant substitution, not a re-span.

challenges.claim: The row's stated tier-1 device — quotation marks setting off web:Ps.22.8 — exists only in the English witness, since MT carries no speech-introducing verb at the seam and the staged extract has no quotation layer.
challenges.evidence: WEB supplies the frame: “They shake their heads, saying,” (web:Ps.22.7) and the quotation marks around “"He trusts in Yahweh. Let him deliver him. Let him rescue him, since he delights in him."” (web:Ps.22.8). MT oshb:Ps.22.8 (= web:Ps.22.7; 7+1=8) ends יָנִ֥יעוּ רֹֽאשׁ with no verb of speaking, and the taunt at oshb:Ps.22.9 (= web:Ps.22.8; 8+1=9) opens asyndetically with גֹּ֣ל, a 2ms imperative that WEB renders as an indicative statement. The OL-grade discourse frame available here is the jussive chain יְפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ יַ֝צִּילֵ֗הוּ at oshb:Ps.22.9. Hebrew runs spliced from verse_map_oshb; collate.py returns tier "byte" for each against the ref cited. Not contested: the addressee shift the row also cites is real — sweep of the WEB tokens you/your across web:Ps.22.6-Ps.22.8 returns 0 of 3 verses.

reviews.reasoning: Both dual-cites are correct (9+1=10, 11+1=12) and the 11|12 seam itself stands: the you/your sweep returns 0 of 3 verses across web:Ps.22.12-Ps.22.14, so the address really does lapse immediately after the span. Two evidence defects sit on top of that sound seam. The row's one digit-bearing signal names the WEB tokens you/your as its object and reports 3 of 3 verses; the re-derived figure is 2 of 3. And the rejected alternative is dismissed with a universal that the bytes falsify four verses later. Neither defect moves the boundary, but both are load-bearing prose: the first is the row's only quantified evidence, the second is its whole ground for preferring this seam over the merge.

challenges.claim: The row's only digit-bearing signal names the WEB tokens you/your and claims them in 3 of 3 verses; the sweep returns 2 of 3, and the missing verse carries no 2ms pronoun or suffix in MT either.
challenges.evidence: Sweep of the WEB word-tokens you/your (unit: verses containing at least one hit) across web:Ps.22.9-Ps.22.11 returns 2 verses of 3 — hits at web:Ps.22.9 and web:Ps.22.10, none at web:Ps.22.11, which reads “Don't be far from me, for trouble is near. For there is no one to help.” (web:Ps.22.11). MT oshb:Ps.22.12 (= web:Ps.22.11; 11+1=12) opens אַל תִּרְחַ֣ק מִ֭מֶּנִּי: the address there is carried by the negated 2ms jussive alone, with no independent pronoun and no 2ms suffix, so the row's named evidence object is absent in both witnesses at that verse. The underlying analytic point — second-person address continues through the span — is sustainable on the verb form; the stated count is not.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative asserts that address to God 'drops out entirely' from web:Ps.22.12 onward, an unswept universal that the bytes falsify at web:Ps.22.15.
challenges.evidence: Within the block the row says the address vacates, web:Ps.22.15 reads “You have brought me into the dust of death.” (web:Ps.22.15). MT oshb:Ps.22.16 (= web:Ps.22.15; 15+1=16) closes וְֽלַעֲפַר מָ֥וֶת תִּשְׁפְּתֵֽנִי, a prefix-conjugation form with 1cs suffix that WEB reads as 2ms. Sweep of the WEB tokens you/your across web:Ps.22.12-Ps.22.18: 1 verse of 7 (web:Ps.22.15). The seam at 11|12 is untouched by this — web:Ps.22.12-Ps.22.14 return 0 of 3 — but the universal as written is false, and the same premise recurs on the far side of the seam, so the cure is one edit installed on both rows.

reviews.reasoning: Dual-cites are correct (12+1=13, 18+1=19) and the span tiles cleanly, but the row's cohesion warrant is factually wrong inside its own span. The row rests the whole 7-verse block on there being no direct second-person address to God across it; web:Ps.22.15 addresses God directly. That single fact does double damage: it voids the driver, and it voids the reason given for rejecting the sub-split, because the address shift the row says is absent is exactly the tier-1 marker a rival seam would use. I am not asserting the split must be made — the imagery does run continuously and the medium confidence is honest — but the rival cannot be dismissed on a claim the bytes contradict, and a replacement warrant has to pass the test that killed this one. Separately noted, not filed: the row states the WEB reading at web:Ps.22.16 as content while disclosing the variance only through a WEB footnote, where MT oshb:Ps.22.17 reads כָּ֝אֲרִ֗י יָדַ֥י וְרַגְלָֽי with no piercing verb; the disclosure is adequate as written, and a challenge resting on the footnote alone would be tier-4-grounded.

challenges.claim: The row's stated cohesion driver — that no direct second-person address to God occurs across web:Ps.22.12-Ps.22.18 — is contradicted inside the span at web:Ps.22.15.

Sweep of the WEB word-tokens you/your (unit: verses) across the row's own span web:Ps.22.12-Ps.22.18 returns 1 verse of 7, at web:Ps.22.15; the row's claim requires 0 of 7. MT oshb:Ps.22.16 (= web:Ps.22.15; 15+1=16) reads in full יָ֘בֵ֤שׁ כַּחֶ֨רֶשׂ כֹּחִ֗י וּ֭לְשׁוֹנִי מֻדְבָּ֣ק מַלְקוֹחָ֑י וְֽלַעֲפַר מָ֥וֶת תִּשְׁפְּתֵֽנִי, closing on a prefix-conjugation form with 1cs suffix that WEB reads as 2ms address to God. Hebrew spliced from verse_map_oshb, collate tier "byte" against oshb:Ps.22.16. Because observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of the driver, the warrant needs re-authoring rather than a patch.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative dismisses the sub-split for want of an address shift inside the span, when that shift stands one verse past the seam it weighed, leaving web:Ps.22.14|web:Ps.22.15 a live rival.
challenges.evidence: The row weighs a split at web:Ps.22.14 and rejects it because no address shift or formal marker sits inside the span; the shift is at web:Ps.22.15, “You have brought me into the dust of death.” (web:Ps.22.15 = oshb:Ps.22.16, 15+1=16, closing token תִּשְׁפְּתֵֽנִי). It divides the predator imagery of web:Ps.22.12-Ps.22.14 (you/your sweep: 0 of 3 verses) from the body-and-death imagery that follows. The rival may still lose on the continuity of the catalog, but it has to be refused on a true premise.

reviews.reasoning: The original-language spine of this row is sound. The Hebrew quote collates at BYTE tier and is verse-initial at the ref cited: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה opens oshb:Ps.22.20 (= web:Ps.22.19), and it does echo וְאַתָּ֥ה קָד֑וֹשׁ at oshb:Ps.22.4 (= web:Ps.22.3); the row says 'the same contrastive formula' rather than claiming byte identity, which is correct discipline, since the two differ in accent. All three dual-cites are right (19+1=20, 3+1=4, 21+1=22), and the closing claim that the verb turns from plea to completed action is byte-supported: oshb:Ps.22.22 (= web:Ps.22.21) ends עֲנִיתָֽנִי, a qatal with 1cs suffix, against the imperatives that precede it. The defect is in the one quantified signal: a raw consonantal-substring count is presented as a count of the formula, and the swept spelling is never named — the documented short-token hazard of this book.

challenges.claim: The signal's book-wide figure of 23 verses is a raw consonantal-substring count, not a count of the contrastive formula: one of the 23 verses carries the string only as bound material inside a longer verb, so the formula figure is 22 verses.
challenges.evidence: sweep.py --skel on the token spliced from oshb:Ps.22.4 (וְאַתָּ֥ה, skeleton ואתה) returns 23 verses and 23 token occurrences book-wide. Token-by-token inspection of those 23: 22 verses carry the free pronoun as a whole token, while oshb:Ps.119.45 (= web:Ps.119.45, an identity psalm) carries וְאֶתְהַלְּכָ֥ה, a hitpael cohortative in which the string is a substring of a longer form. Formula count: 22 verses, 22 occurrences; substring count: 23 verses, 23 occurrences. The in-psalm half of the signal is correct and I confirm it — exactly 2 verses inside Psalm 22, oshb:Ps.22.4 (= web:Ps.22.3; 3+1=4) and oshb:Ps.22.20 (= web:Ps.22.19; 19+1=20), one at each renewed address. Naming the swept object as a spelling first, per count-object discipline, is what keeps a spelling count from standing in for a formula count.

reviews.reasoning: This row handles a genuinely contested strophe seam about as honestly as the evidence allows: it opens the vow unit at the pivot, concedes in the rejected alternative that the rival attachment cannot be excluded on the bytes, and prices that with medium confidence. Dual-cites are correct (22+1=23, 26+1=27), the ellipsis quotation at web:Ps.22.26 matches the WEB text on both sides of the elision under check_web_quotes, and the row makes no hallelu-Yah claim at oshb:Ps.22.27 (= web:Ps.22.26), where יְהַֽלְל֣וּ יְ֭הוָה is a skeleton collision rather than the frame. The signal cites only the first verb as cohortative and is right to. The defect is confined to the rejected alternative, which extends the form label across both verbs; the register argument survives on the first, so severity is low.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative rests the seam on 'cohortative' verbs at web:Ps.22.22, but only the first of the two verbs it cites is a cohortative form; the second cannot carry the cohortative marker.
challenges.evidence: MT oshb:Ps.22.23 (= web:Ps.22.22; 22+1=23) reads אֲסַפְּרָ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֣ לְאֶחָ֑י בְּת֖וֹךְ קָהָ֣ל אֲהַלְלֶֽךָּ. The first verb אֲסַפְּרָ֣ה carries the paragogic he and is cohortative, rendered “I will declare your name to my brothers.” (web:Ps.22.22). The second, אֲהַלְלֶֽךָּ, rendered “Among the assembly, I will praise you.” (web:Ps.22.22), is a 1cs prefix form with a 2ms object suffix and is not marked as a cohortative — the paragogic he does not co-occur with the object suffix. Hebrew spliced from verse_map_oshb, collate tier "byte" against oshb:Ps.22.23. The volitive register the row argues is real on the first verb; the row carries 0 Hebrew runs in any field to support what is a form-grade claim.

reviews.reasoning: The seam is well founded and the row reads it correctly. MT oshb:Ps.22.28 (= web:Ps.22.27; 27+1=28) opens יִזְכְּר֤וּ וְיָשֻׁ֣בוּ אֶל יְ֭הוָה כָּל אַפְסֵי אָ֑רֶץ — the turn to the ends of the earth is carried by the Hebrew clause itself, not only by the English, and WEB renders it “All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to Yahweh.” (web:Ps.22.27). The contrast the row draws against the assembly-scoped vocabulary of the preceding strophe holds at both poles, each quotation matching its cited verse under check_web_quotes. Its 1 dual-cite carries correct arithmetic (26+1=27). Two things I checked and found clean rather than defective: the refs array holds no ref inside the row's own span, which is permitted here because the row makes no original-language citation that would trigger a dual-cite and in-span prose refs are exempt from the mirror requirement; and web:Ps.22.30 reads “the Lord” for MT לַֽאדֹנָ֣י at oshb:Ps.22.31, which is Adonai in the source and therefore not the 68:26-class rendering zone — the row rightly claims nothing about it. Confidence high is earned.

The numbering handling is exactly right, which is the whole risk on a whole-psalm row in this book. Psalm 23 is an identity psalm and its title is not separately counted: verse_map_web carries Ps.23.0 with mt "inside Ps.23.1" and an empty mt_title_verses, the device inventory records the superscription as prefix_of_v1, and the bytes show it — oshb:Ps.23.1 reads מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִ֑ד יְהוָ֥ה רֹ֝עִ֗י לֹ֣א אֶחְסָֽר, title and first colon in one verse. So the row's claim that the title sits inside MT verse 1 is byte-true, and web:Ps.23.0 = oshb:Ps.23.1 is the owner-ruled form; the remaining cites are identity-correct. Span is 6 verses in both witnesses and tiles the psalm exactly. The rejected alternative is the right one to weigh and is refused on true premises: the person shift it names is real — oshb:Ps.23.4 carries כִּי אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּדִ֑י, rendered “for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.” (web:Ps.23.4) — and the row types it as texture rather than a formal seam, correctly, since pmarks_Ps.json carries no Ps.23 selah key and the psalm has no refrain and no vocative opener. The short-psalm appeal is grounded rather than invented: the governing row-granularity rule covers indivisible psalms of roughly eight verses or fewer, and this is six. Noted, not filed: the title-inside-v1 point is an original-language structural claim carried without a Hebrew quote, though it is true and machine-checkable as written.
